headline: Today's developments feature new open-source security tools like OpenAI and Cisco's Shirudo, alongside research in 3D world modeling, robotic manipulation training, and AI agents designed for gaming and customer support.

items.title: Plan4D: Generative Plannable 4D Worlds
items.summary: Plan4D is a generative world model designed to predict future RGB videos along with dense 4D geometry, including depth, cameras, and point clouds. By combining foundational video generators and 3D reconstructors using a model-stitching architecture, it enables long-horizon action planning in dynamic 3D environments.
items.why_it_matters: It improves the physical and geometric accuracy of AI-generated future video scenes.

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduced Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps protect running Linux systems while patches are being deployed. It uses Linux eBPF technology and AI-generated shields to block exploits on active services without requiring system restarts.
items.why_it_matters: It offers security teams a way to temporarily mitigate vulnerabilities in running systems without taking services offline.

items.title: Connected intelligence for in-house legal
items.summary: A video discussion hosted by OpenAI features industry professionals exploring how artificial intelligence can assist in-house legal teams. The panel covers connecting business context, building reusable workflows, and managing outside counsel.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights practical applications and workflow strategies for AI adoption in legal departments.

items.title: Richpanel helps companies automate 50% of support in 30 days
items.summary: Richpanel uses various OpenAI models to automate customer support operations for companies. The system uses specialized models to automatically set up agent tools and procedures, while utilizing more cost-efficient models to handle everyday customer conversations.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates how companies can combine different AI models to balance intelligence and operating costs in customer service.

items.title: A Glimpse of Training VLMs as Foundation Models for Robotic Manipulation
items.summary: Researchers introduce nanoAstra, a method for training vision-language models for robotic manipulation by combining semantic action modeling with capability-preserving supervised fine-tuning. The 9-billion parameter model outperforms existing baselines on a randomized benchmark and supports fast streaming execution.
items.why_it_matters: It demonstrates a way to train generalizable robot control models that reduce a robot's idle time and improve zero-shot success rates.

items.title: Developing-Gamer/agent-sim: iOS simulators for AI agents, on Linux
items.summary: This project runs Apple's iOS simulator runtime on ordinary Linux machines without requiring a Mac or GPU. It provides tools for AI agents to test iOS apps by reading the screen, tapping, typing, and viewing the live stream in a browser.
items.why_it_matters: It allows AI agents running on Linux to test and interact with iOS applications directly.

items.title: WeightCode: Installing New Capabilities into Neural Networks via Weight-Space Programming
items.summary: The paper explores Weight-Space Programming (WSP), where executable programs directly modify a neural network's weights to install new capabilities without gradient-based training. Using a frozen language model to write these weight programs, the framework achieves high success rates on command compositions and vision tasks while preserving original capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: It introduces a new route to acquiring and accumulating capabilities in trained neural networks by writing directly to their weight space.

items.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
items.summary: The authors introduce AutoPILOT, a visual agent harness for real-time video games that allows models to output primitive actions, macros, or closed-loop controllers instead of just a single action per model call. Tested on a new benchmark of 120 browser games, AutoPILOT significantly improves success rates in real-time environments compared to existing harnesses.
items.why_it_matters: It addresses the limitation of AI agents in real-time settings by changing how model outputs are converted into ongoing actions over time.

items.title: Self-WSP: Can Language Models Improve Themselves Through Weight-Space Programming?
items.summary: This paper investigates Self-WSP, an approach where a language model reads and edits its own weights using Weight-Space Programming to try to improve itself. While self-edits substantially raised accuracy on math benchmarks, further analysis showed the model lacked interpretability regarding the changes it made, as random search sometimes performed similarly.
items.why_it_matters: It offers insight into recursive self-improvement for language models while highlighting current limitations in the interpretability of self-edited weights.

items.title: Autoregressive View Model
items.summary: Researchers present the Autoregressive View Model (AVM), which generates a scene as a stream of views without needing an explicit 3D representation. The model conditions on images or videos to generate short clips along a requested camera path, and uses a fine-tuned bidirectional video diffusion transformer scaled across roughly 8 million scenes. Results show that AVM adapts to various input and output settings through a single in-context interface.
items.why_it_matters: It introduces a new way to handle scene generation and camera control without building an explicit 3D model first.

items.title: Seeing the Invisible: How Vision-Language Models Read, Predict and Trace Radio Fields
items.summary: This paper investigates whether vision-language models can infer invisible radio fields in a city based only on visible structures like buildings and streets. The authors built RadioVISTA, a label-free engine and benchmark to test this physical reasoning. Their evaluations reveal that while frontier models can judge where a radio field is strong, they struggle to trace specific underlying paths.
items.why_it_matters: It highlights a gap in how vision-language models perform physical reasoning about invisible elements in the real world.

items.title: From Points to Trajectories: Rethinking Multimodal Alignment for Physical Events
items.summary: The authors examine physical artificial intelligence and how multimodal aligners capture real-world mechanics over time. They show that traditional temporal pooling averages out transient dynamics, making it impossible to distinguish between distinct physical executions under identical conditions. To fix this, they introduce CounterPoint, a plug-in module that scores frame-level cross-modal agreement.
items.why_it_matters: It identifies a fundamental limitation in how multimodal models process physical events over time and proposes a fix for fine-grained alignment.

items.title: How Feedback-Free Self-Evolution Reshapes Agent Skills: A Systematic Study
items.summary: This study explores how agent skills—documents containing procedural knowledge—evolve when models rewrite them repeatedly without external task feedback. The experiments show that letting models rewrite expert skills without feedback causes the skills to lose value and erode expert knowledge over time. Based on this, the authors introduce a method called SkillDiff that preserves crucial expert knowledge and improves agent performance.
items.why_it_matters: It uncovers a risk in letting AI agents autonomously update their own procedural knowledge without feedback and offers a way to retain expert insights.

items.title: GameAnything: From Any Inspirations to Playable Game Worlds
items.summary: The authors introduce GameAnything, an open-source agentic platform that turns multimodal inspirations into playable extensions of existing games through iterative development. They also present GameAnything-Bench, a benchmark used to assess functional correctness and gameplay quality across diverse references and environments. Evaluations show that current coding agents can adapt reference content, but still struggle with playable interactions.
items.why_it_matters: It provides an open-source platform and benchmark for AI-driven, inspiration-based game development.

items.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
items.summary: Researchers introduce Doppeldwarf-306, a benchmark of nearly 1,700 photographs of bronze dwarf statues in Poland to test how well visual retrieval systems can distinguish nearly identical objects. Using frozen image features without any training, a baseline search correctly identifies the right statue up to 94.7% of the time, and incorporating location data or learned feature matching further improves accuracy.
items.why_it_matters: It provides a new way to test and improve how computer vision models tell apart very similar physical objects.
